name: CDS
frequency: Twice a year (CDS I and CDS II)
approxCandidates: ≈2–4 lakh applicants per cycle (approx.); about 450–460 vacancies per cycle across IMA, INA, AFA and OTA
eligibility: Graduate. INA needs an engineering degree, and AFA needs a degree with Physics and Maths at Class 12 or an engineering degree. Age is about 19–25 depending on the academy, unmarried for IMA/INA/AFA

notification.summary: CDS (II) 2026 was held on 13 September 2026, and its written result is expected in October 2026. Per UPSC's Calendar 2027, the CDS (I) 2027 notification is due on 2 December 2026 (applications until 22 December 2026) and the exam on 11 April 2027. Dates are provisional; upsc.gov.in itself could not be reached from the research sandbox.

pattern.notes: There are three papers of 2 hours and 100 marks each. English and GK have 120 questions each (100/120 ≈ 0.83 marks per question) and Elementary Maths has 100 (1 mark each). A wrong answer costs one-third of the question's marks. OTA (SSC) candidates take only English and GK (200 marks). The SSB interview follows. The bank holds 60 items, 20 per paper; for a short mock, score each paper with its own per-question marks as given in sections[].marking.

trendAnalysis.summary: English is moderate. Error spotting, comprehension and sentence or part ordering are about half the paper, and the vocabulary items (synonyms, antonyms, idioms) are of mid-level difficulty. GK is the most unpredictable paper: History, Geography and Polity are the static core, science is mostly Physics and Biology basics, and there are many questions on current affairs, defence exercises and international organisations. Elementary Maths stays at Class 10 level with an even spread across arithmetic, algebra, geometry, mensuration and trigonometry, but it is lengthy. Over 2024–26, GK difficulty has been moderate-to-tough while Maths and English stayed moderate.

resources.notes: UPSC posts CDS question papers on upsc.gov.in under Previous Question Papers. Answer keys are released only after the final result of that cycle.

pyqBlueprint.method: Built from the official CDS (I) and (II) question papers that UPSC publishes, and from post-exam analyses (SSBCrack, Physics Wallah, PWOnlyIAS, Careers360) for 2024–2025. For example, the CDS 1 2025 English paper was dominated by spotting errors, idioms, fill in the blanks and word or sentence ordering, while synonyms, antonyms and RC returned in other sittings. 2026 is covered from memory-based analyses and the writer's own knowledge; topic tables could not be fetched, and WebSearch gave only summaries. Each archetype is a recurring format described in our own words.

archetypes.pattern: Sentence in parts (a)(b)(c) + 'No error': agreement traps ('each of', 'either … or', 'neither of', 'one of').
Spotting errors in prepositions/idiomatic usage ('despite of', 'discuss about'), tense, stative verbs, and 'hardly … when'.
Synonym of a mid-level word (ostensible, laconic, acrimonious); distractors include an antonym and a look-alike.
Antonym of a mid-level word (obdurate, ephemeral, frugal); one distractor is a synonym.
Vocabulary blank: choose the contextually apt adjective/noun from near-synonyms.
Grammar blank: preposition after an adjective/verb (senior to, prefer to, since/for), fixed phrases.
Replace the underlined part or choose 'No improvement': gerund after 'look forward to', 'insist on', 'no sooner … than', agreement.
Rearrange parts P, Q, R (S) of a sentence into the correct order.
Ordering of sentences: S1 and S6 fixed, arrange P, Q, R, S into a coherent paragraph.
Passage of 150–250 words with a central-idea or inference question.
Passage-based factual detail or word-in-context meaning question.
Meaning of a common idiom or phrasal expression; distractors take the literal meaning.
Cloze passage with numbered blanks: pick the word that fits meaning and collocation.
Ancient and medieval India: rulers, monuments, texts and dynasties (Chola navy, Arthashastra, Buland Darwaza).
Modern India and the national movement: parties, missions, battles, revolutionary organisations and founders.
Indian geography: peaks, rivers, boundaries and lines (McMahon, Radcliffe), neighbours.
World and physical geography: pressure belts, Ring of Fire, landlocked countries, winds.
Constitutional articles, sources and amendments (DPSP source, Art 32, 61st Amendment).
Institutions and procedures: joint sitting, CAG reports, presiding officers.
Economic concepts and institutions: GDP deflator, RBI functions, inflation index used for targeting.
Everyday physics: optics (mirrors, refraction), waves, units and energy conversions.
Allotropes, common gases and compounds and their properties.
Human physiology and diseases: pathogens, organs, brain parts, vitamins.
Environmental conventions, ozone depletion, biodiversity hotspots.
Defence institutions, gallantry awards and military training establishments.
Military exercises and their partner countries.
International organisations and their headquarters/functions.
Number properties: trailing zeros, remainders, unit digits, divisibility tests.
HCF/LCM applications: product rule, greatest number leaving the same remainder.
Percentage and profit–loss–discount: successive transactions, consumption adjustment, mark-up with discount.
Simple and compound interest, including CI − SI for 2 years.
Ratio and proportion: compound ratios, dividing a sum in a chained ratio.
Time and work, and pipes and cisterns, with combined rates.
Speed–distance: trains crossing, boats and streams, relative speed.
Algebraic identities: x + 1/x, a³ − b³, a + b + c = 0 and simplifying rational expressions.
Linear and quadratic equations: solving systems, roots and coefficients.
Triangles and circles: angle bisector angles, BPT, tangents, angles subtended by chords.
Polygons and quadrilaterals: interior/exterior angle sums, number of sides.
2D mensuration: areas of triangles, circles and quadrilaterals.
3D mensuration: cubes, cylinders, spheres, including melting and recasting.
Trigonometric identities and values given one ratio.
Heights and distances with 30°/45°/60° angles.
Mean, median and mode from raw data, including corrected mean after a misread value.

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Each of the candidates (A) / have been given (B) / a separate room. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'Each of' takes a singular verb, so part B should read 'has been given'.

relevance.note: 'Each of…have' agreement is an exact CDS error-spotting item

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
She has been working here (A) / for the last five years (B) / and is knowing everyone. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and is not normally used in the continuous form, so part C should read 'and knows everyone'.

relevance.note: Stative 'is knowing' error matches CDS E02

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to OSTENSIBLE.
questions.explanation: Ostensible means apparent or seeming on the surface, though perhaps not actually so.

relevance.note: OSTENSIBLE synonym with 'hidden' antonym is classic CDS vocab

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to LACONIC.
questions.explanation: Laconic means using very few words, that is, terse.

relevance.note: LACONIC/terse with 'verbose' antonym and 'lazy' look-alike matches CDS

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to OBDURATE.
questions.explanation: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change, so its opposite is yielding. The other options are near-synonyms.

relevance.note: OBDURATE antonym with three synonym decoys is CDS-standard

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The veteran's account of the war was so ______ that many in the audience were moved to tears.
questions.explanation: Poignant means evoking a keen sense of sadness, which fits 'moved to tears'.

relevance.note: Poignant vs pedantic/prosaic/perfunctory p-word set is very CDS-like

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'The officer insisted on me to stay back.' (underlined: insisted on me to stay)
questions.explanation: 'Insist' is followed by 'on + gerund' ('insisted on my staying') or a that-clause ('insisted that I stay'). Of the options, only 'insisted that I stay' is correct.

relevance.note: 'insisted that I stay' improvement is CDS-type

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'The number of cadets who passed the test are higher this year.' (underlined: are higher)
questions.explanation: 'The number of …' is singular and the sentence is in the present ('this year'), so 'is higher' is correct.

relevance.note: 'The number of…is' improvement is a CDS agreement favourite

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'Military historians often observe that battles are seldom won by numbers alone. An army that is well supplied, well led and confident of its purpose can defeat a larger force that lacks these qualities. Leadership, in this view, is less about issuing orders than about earning trust: soldiers willingly follow a commander who shares their hardships and explains the reasons behind difficult decisions. Such trust cannot be created on the eve of battle; it is built slowly, through countless small acts of fairness in peacetime.'
Which of the following best expresses the central idea of the passage?
options: Commanders should avoid explaining their decisions
Effective leadership rests on trust earned over time
questions.explanation: The passage argues that leadership means earning trust built over time. It rejects the idea that numbers alone decide battles.

relevance.note: Central-idea RC with clear distractors fits CDS

questions.question: Which of the following rulers was NOT part of the alliance that fought the English East India Company at the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
questions.explanation: At Buxar the Company fought the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh) and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. Haider Ali of Mysore was not involved.

relevance.note: Buxar alliance 'NOT' pick with Haider Ali is a good CDS item

questions.question: The 'Doldrums' are associated with which pressure belt?
questions.explanation: The doldrums are the calm equatorial low-pressure zone where the trade winds converge (the ITCZ).

relevance.note: Doldrums-equatorial low fits CDS world geography

questions.question: The GDP deflator is the ratio of:
questions.explanation: GDP deflator = (nominal GDP / real GDP) × 100. It is a broad measure of the price level.

relevance.note: GDP deflator ratio matches CDS G07

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT an allotrope of carbon?
questions.explanation: Carborundum is silicon carbide (SiC), a compound, not an allotrope. Diamond, graphite and fullerenes are allotropes of carbon.

relevance.note: Carborundum not an allotrope is a CDS-type trap

questions.question: How many zeros are there at the end of 100! (100 factorial)?
questions.explanation: The number of trailing zeros is ⌊100/5⌋ + ⌊100/25⌋ = 20 + 4 = 24.

relevance.note: Trailing zeros of 100! is a CDS staple

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2³¹ is divided by 5?
questions.explanation: Powers of 2 mod 5 cycle as 2, 4, 3, 1 (period 4). Since 31 = 4 × 7 + 3, 2³¹ ≡ 2³ = 8 ≡ 3 (mod 5).

relevance.note: Cyclicity remainder 2^31 mod 5 is CDS-type

questions.question: If the price of sugar rises by 25%, by what percentage must a family reduce its consumption so that its expenditure on sugar stays the same?

relevance.note: Consumption adjustment 25%→20% is classic CDS

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. His profit per cent is:
questions.explanation: SP = 1.40 × 0.90 × CP = 1.26 × CP, so the profit is 26%.

relevance.note: Markup-discount profit is CDS M03

questions.question: A train 150 m long runs at 54 km/h. How long will it take to cross a bridge 300 m long?
questions.explanation: 54 km/h = 15 m/s. The distance to cover is 150 + 300 = 450 m, so time = 450/15 = 30 s.

relevance.note: Train crossing bridge with length trap is CDS standard

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 3, then x³ + 1/x³ equals:

relevance.note: x+1/x cube identity is CDS M08

questions.question: In triangle ABC, ∠A = 50°. The bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at I. The measure of ∠BIC is:

relevance.note: ∠BIC = 90+A/2 is a CDS geometry favourite

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Either the manager or his assistants (A) / is responsible (B) / for the loss of the files. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: With 'either … or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Assistants' is plural, so part B should be 'are responsible'.

relevance.note: Either-or proximity agreement is exact CDS E01

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The committee has (A) / discussed about the proposal (B) / in great detail. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'Discuss' is a transitive verb and takes a direct object: 'discussed the proposal'. 'About' is superfluous.

relevance.note: 'discussed about' is a CDS-named error

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Hardly had he entered the room (A) / than the lights (B) / went out. (C) / No error (D)
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' is followed by 'when' (or 'before'), not 'than'. 'Than' goes with 'no sooner'.

relevance.note: 'Hardly…than' error matches CDS E02

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning to ACRIMONIOUS.
questions.explanation: Acrimonious means angry and bitter (an acrimonious debate). Cordial is its opposite.

relevance.note: ACRIMONIOUS with 'cordial' antonym decoy is CDS-faithful

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to FRUGAL.
questions.explanation: Frugal means sparing with money; extravagant means spending wastefully. Thrifty is a synonym.

relevance.note: FRUGAL antonym with synonym decoys is named CDS item

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to TACITURN.
questions.explanation: Taciturn means saying little; talkative is the opposite. Reserved is a near-synonym.

relevance.note: TACITURN antonym fits CDS

questions.question: Fill in the blank: He prefers tea ______ coffee.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to' when comparing two things: prefer tea to coffee.

relevance.note: 'prefer…to' is named CDS item

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'No sooner had the bell rung than the students rushed out.' (underlined: had the bell rung than)
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' takes inversion with the past perfect and is followed by 'than'. The sentence is already correct.

relevance.note: Correct 'No sooner…than' as No-improvement is a CDS trap

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the underlined part. If none is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
'I am looking forward to meet you at the passing-out parade.' (underlined: to meet)
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund: 'looking forward to meeting you'.

relevance.note: 'looking forward to meeting' is exact CDS E07

questions.question:
The first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) of a passage are given. Arrange P, Q, R and S in the proper order.
S1: Ravi joined the army at the age of nineteen.
P: After years of hard work, he was promoted to the rank of Havildar.
Q: His first posting was in the cold desert of Ladakh.
R: There he learnt to survive in extreme conditions.
S: That experience later helped him win the respect of his seniors.
S6: Today he trains young recruits in the same regiment.
questions.explanation: Q (first posting) leads to R ('There' = Ladakh), R to S ('That experience'), and S to P (promotion after years of work), which connects to S6 (training recruits today).

relevance.note: S1/S6 paragraph ordering matches CDS E09 format

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'In many villages near forests, conflict between people and wild animals has grown as farmland expands into former habitats. Elephants raid crops, and leopards sometimes prey on livestock. Earlier responses relied on capturing or killing the "problem" animal, but such measures rarely solved the problem for long, since other animals soon moved into the vacant territory. Conservationists now favour approaches that change the circumstances of the conflict: early-warning systems that alert villagers when elephants approach, insurance and prompt compensation for losses, and corridors that allow animals to move between forest patches without crossing fields. These methods demand patience and local cooperation, yet they address the causes rather than the symptoms.'
The central idea of the passage is that human–wildlife conflict is best reduced by:
options: removing every animal that damages crops
measures that address its underlying causes with community cooperation
relying only on compensation for losses
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts removing animals (which treats symptoms) with early warning, compensation and corridors that 'address the causes'. Compensation is only one part of that approach.

relevance.note: Central-idea RC on human-wildlife conflict fits CDS

questions.question: The Chola ruler who sent a naval expedition against the Srivijaya kingdom of South-East Asia was:
questions.explanation: Rajendra I (c. 1014–1044) led the naval campaign against Srivijaya around 1025. Rajaraja I had earlier conquered northern Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

relevance.note: Rajendra I Srivijaya expedition is CDS-typical

questions.question: The Ghadar Party, founded in 1913 on the Pacific coast of North America, is particularly associated with:
questions.explanation: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 by Indian immigrants led by Sohan Singh Bhakna and Lala Har Dayal, who edited its paper 'Ghadar'. The other three were not its founders.

relevance.note: Ghadar-Har Dayal is CDS modern history

questions.question: Which is the highest peak of peninsular India?
questions.explanation: Anamudi (2,695 m) in the Anaimalai Hills of Kerala is the highest peak south of the Himalaya. Doddabetta is the highest in the Nilgiris.

relevance.note: Anamudi with Doddabetta trap is CDS-type

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years?
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment (1988, in force 1989) amended Article 326 to lower the voting age to 18.

relevance.note: 61st Amdt voting age is a recurring CDS item

questions.question: The reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to:
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Under Article 151, the CAG submits Union audit reports to the President, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament.

relevance.note: CAG reports to President is CDS G06

questions.question: Under India's flexible inflation-targeting framework, the inflation target is set in terms of the:
options: Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers
questions.explanation: The target of 4% (with a band of 2–6%) is defined on headline CPI (Combined) inflation, released by the National Statistics Office.

relevance.note: CPI-C inflation target is CDS G07

questions.question: Which one of the following biodiversity hotspots lies partly in India?
options: Madagascar and the Indian Ocean Islands
questions.explanation: India has parts of four hotspots: the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).

relevance.note: Indo-Burma hotspot pick fits CDS environment

questions.question: The Defence Services Staff College is located at:
questions.explanation: DSSC is at Wellington in the Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu. Mhow has the Army War College and Secunderabad the College of Defence Management.

relevance.note: DSSC Wellington is a CDS defence item

questions.question: 'Malabar' is a naval exercise involving the navies of:
options: India, the USA, Japan and Australia
questions.explanation: Malabar began as an India–US exercise; Japan became a permanent participant in 2015 and Australia rejoined in 2020.

relevance.note: Malabar Quad navies matches CDS exercises

questions.question: The unit digit of 7⁹⁵ is:
questions.explanation: Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat in the cycle 7, 9, 3, 1. 95 = 4 × 23 + 3, so the unit digit is the third in the cycle: 3.

relevance.note: Unit digit cyclicity is CDS staple

questions.question: The greatest number that divides 43, 91 and 183, leaving the same remainder in each case, is:

relevance.note: Same-remainder HCF of differences is CDS M02 classic

questions.question: A sells an article to B at a profit of 20%, and B sells it to C at a profit of 10%. If C pays ₹264, what did A pay for it?

relevance.note: Successive profit back-calc is CDS-typical

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹5,000 for 2 years at 8% per annum is:

relevance.note: CI−SI = P(r/100)² is a named CDS item

questions.question: A boat covers 24 km downstream in 2 hours and returns upstream in 4 hours. The speed of the stream is:
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 12 km/h, upstream = 6 km/h. Stream speed = (12 − 6)/2 = 3 km/h.

relevance.note: Boat-stream speed fits CDS

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively, and pipe C can empty it in 15 minutes. If all three are opened together, the empty tank will be filled in:

relevance.note: Fill-and-empty pipes combined is CDS M06

questions.question: ₹7,700 is divided among A, B and C such that A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5. C's share is:

relevance.note: Chained-ratio division of 7700 fits CDS M05

questions.question: If a − b = 4 and ab = 21, then a³ − b³ equals:

relevance.note: a³−b³ via identity fits CDS

questions.question: (x² − 9)/(x² + 5x + 6) simplifies to:
questions.explanation: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) and x² + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3). Cancelling (x + 3) gives (x − 3)/(x + 2).

relevance.note: Factor-cancel rational expression is CDS-type

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O, and ∠AOB = 110°. If C is a point on the major arc, then ∠ACB is:
questions.explanation: The angle subtended at the circumference on the major arc is half the central angle: 110°/2 = 55°. (125° is the angle on the minor arc.)

relevance.note: Inscribed angle half central is CDS

questions.question: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into a solid cylinder of radius 4 cm. The height of the cylinder is:
questions.explanation: (4/3)π(6³) = π(4²)h, so 288π = 16πh and h = 18 cm.

relevance.note: Sphere recast into cylinder is CDS M13 classic

questions.question: The mean of 10 observations is 15. Later it was found that one observation, 26, had been wrongly recorded as 16. The correct mean is:
questions.explanation: Recorded sum = 150. Correct sum = 150 − 16 + 26 = 160, so the correct mean = 16.

relevance.note: Corrected mean after misread value is named CDS M16
